components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single primary action in a dialog.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { font-family: var(--font-sans, 'Geist Variable', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif); height: 36px; padding: 8px 16px; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 8px; background: var(--primary); color: var(--primary-ink); font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; transition: all 150ms; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--primary) 90%, transparent); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; border-color: var(--ring); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklch, var(--ring) 50%, transparent); }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: A secondary action that needs a visible edge.
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { font-family: var(--font-sans, 'Geist Variable', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif); height: 32px; padding: 0 12px; border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 8px; background: var(--background); color: var(--ink); font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.05); transition: all 150ms; } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background: var(--secondary); } .ds-btn-outline:focus-visible { outline: none; border-color: var(--ring); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklch, var(--ring) 50%, transparent); }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Most buttons in dense rows and menus.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { font-family: var(--font-sans, 'Geist Variable', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif); height: 32px; padding: 0 12px; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 8px; background: transparent; color: var(--ink); font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; transition: all 150ms; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { background: var(--secondary); } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: none; border-color: var(--ring); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklch, var(--ring) 50%, transparent); }

components.name: Text Input
components.css: .ds-input { font-family: var(--font-sans, 'Geist Variable', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif); height: 36px; width: 280px; padding: 4px 12px; border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 8px; background: transparent; color: var(--ink); font-size: 0.875rem; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.05); transition: border-color 150ms, box-shadow 150ms; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: var(--ink-muted); } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: none; border-color: var(--ring); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklch, var(--ring) 50%, transparent); }

components.name: Agent Status Dot
components.description: The signature status indicator: amber and red pulse with a ring, working pulses slowly, parked is half-filled, finished is green, idle is a dashed ring.
components.css: .ds-dots { display: flex; gap: 16px; align-items: center; } .ds-dot { position: relative; display: inline-block; width: 10px; height: 10px; box-sizing: border-box; border-radius: 9999px; border: 1.5px solid currentColor; background: currentColor; color: var(--ink-muted); } .ds-dot i { position: absolute; inset: -1.5px; border-radius: 9999px; background: currentColor; opacity: 0.6; animation: ds-ping 1s cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.2, 1) infinite; } .ds-dot-amber { color: var(--pulse-amber); } .ds-dot-red { color: var(--pulse-red); } .ds-dot-green { color: var(--pulse-green); } .ds-dot-half { background: linear-gradient(90deg, currentColor 50%, transparent 50%); } .ds-dot-idle { background: transparent; border-style: dashed; } .ds-dot-working { animation: ds-pulse 3.2s ease-in-out infinite; } @keyframes ds-ping { 75%, 100% { transform: scale(2); opacity: 0; } } @keyframes ds-pulse { 0%, 100% { opacity: 0.9; } 50% { opacity: 0.35; } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-dot { animation: none; } .ds-dot i { display: none; } }

components.name: Record List Row
components.description: A 44px List row: the subject, a Status fact and an action.
components.css: .ds-row { font-family: var(--font-sans, 'Geist Variable', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif); display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 16px; width: 420px; height: 44px; padding: 0 8px; border-radius: 6px; color: var(--ink); font-size: 0.875rem; outline: none; } .ds-row:hover { background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--secondary) 60%, transparent); } .ds-row:focus-visible { box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px var(--ring); } .ds-row-name { flex: 1; font-weight: 600; } .ds-status { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; font-size: 0.75rem; } .ds-status-dot { width: 10px; height: 10px; border-radius: 9999px; background: currentColor; } .ds-row-action { font-family: var(--font-sans, 'Geist Variable', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif); height: 24px; padding: 0 8px; border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 8px; background: var(--background); color: var(--ink); font-size: 0.75rem; }

components.name: Entity
components.description: A hired agent: an initials avatar, the name and the job title.
components.html: SEUnnamed Software engineerSoftware engineer
components.css: .ds-entity { font-family: var(--font-sans, 'Geist Variable', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif); display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; color: var(--ink); font-size: 0.875rem; } .ds-avatar { display: inline-grid; place-items: center; width: 24px; height: 24px; border-radius: 9999px; background: var(--surface); color: var(--ink-muted); font-size: 0.625rem; font-weight: 500; } .ds-entity-desc { color: var(--ink-muted); font-size: 0.75rem; }

components.name: Tooltip
components.description: An inverted label shown on hover or focus.
components.css: .ds-tooltip { font-family: var(--font-sans, 'Geist Variable', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif); display: inline-block; padding: 6px 12px; border-radius: 8px; background: var(--ink); color: var(--background); font-size: 0.75rem; }

narrative.overview:
dia is a polished native desktop app in the lineage of Linear, Arc, and Raycast: crisp, cool-neutral surfaces; deliberate, sparing color; motion that responds to what the user just did rather than performing for its own sake. The user sends agents out to work and does not watch them. The UI's first job is to show, in one list, which agents need the user and what the others are doing, and then to get out of the way: one agent's tab fills the window at a time, and the rest keep working out of view.

The colour palette is named **Control Room**: many status lights on a quiet cool-neutral ground, with one operator watching them. Density is that of a desktop tool: 14px body text, 44px record rows, hairline dividers instead of cards, and one accent.

This system explicitly rejects two adjacent aesthetics: the generic AI-chat-SaaS look (gradient hero treatments, bubbly chat-marketing polish, anything that reads as a hosted product's landing page) and the raw terminal-multiplexer look (bare ASCII borders, zero-chrome, tmux-default starkness). dia is a native app that happens to run agent sessions — not a wrapped terminal, and not a product being sold.
keyCharacteristics: Cool-neutral Control Room palette, in a light and a dark theme, with each color role used deliberately
Sans + mono pairing: sans for chrome and UI copy, mono for session/code content
Amber, red and green carry severity only: amber for a warning or alert, red for an error, green for a finished agent
Records are drawn with the draekien/design-system components (`List`, `Status`, `Entity`, `Figure`, `RelativeTime`) on dia's own tokens
Responsive, non-choreographed motion: transitions confirm actions, they don't perform

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Amber marks every warning and alert. Red marks every error. Green marks a finished agent. No element uses these colours for decoration or emphasis: diff added and removed lines are neither warnings nor errors, so they do not use them. Amber and red pulse only on the status indicator. The OS-drawn close button's red hover is not dia's and does not follow this rule (ADR-0039).

rules.name: The No Middle Dot Rule
rules.body: Text dia writes never uses the middle dot (U+00B7) as a separator. Use layout spacing, a line break, a comma or a sentence instead: `3 steps, Bash failed, 12s`, not the same parts joined by middle dots. Data from elsewhere shown verbatim, such as a skill's `argumentHint`, keeps its own characters.

rules.name: The Content-Is-Mono Rule
rules.body: The agent's *literal output* — code, file paths, tool names, command strings, and other verbatim snippets — renders in the mono family. Everything else, including the agent's *prose* (paragraphs, lists, and headings inside a Markdown message) and all of dia's own chrome (buttons, labels, dialogs), renders in the sans family. The two are never mixed within one span of text: mono is a signal that "this is a literal string," so widening it to whole prose bodies would drain that signal. An overview activity line follows the same rule: a `TodoWrite` item is sans, a tool call such as `Edit src/main/index.ts` is mono.

rules.name: The Flat Frame Rule
rules.body: At rest there is one level. The sidebar and the content area, and the regions inside them, are separated by borders and dividers, not shadows. Elevation appears only in direct response to an open dialog or overlay.

dos: **Do** keep color roles deliberate: primary for action/selection, the cool neutrals for structure, amber for warnings, red for errors and green for a finished agent, per the One Voice Rule.
**Do** use mono for all literal agent/session content and sans for all dia chrome, per the Content-Is-Mono Rule.
**Do** keep to the one resting level, reserving elevation for dialogs and overlays, per the Flat Frame Rule.
**Do** make motion responsive to real actions (tab switch, row selection, status change) — confirm, don't choreograph.
**Do** draw a list of comparable records with `List`, its states with `Status`, people and agents with `Entity`, and compared numbers with `Figure`, per Record lists.
donts: **Don't** build a generic AI-chat-SaaS look — no gradient hero treatments, no bubble-chat marketing polish, nothing that reads as a hosted product's landing page.
**Don't** default to a raw terminal-multiplexer aesthetic — no bare ASCII-art borders, no zero-chrome-for-its-own-sake tmux-default look.
**Don't** use amber, red or green for decoration or emphasis; they mean warning, error and finished.
**Don't** separate text with a middle dot (U+00B7), per the No Middle Dot Rule.
**Don't** pulse for a finished agent; a finished agent does not need the user, and a pulse there makes the needs-input pulse easier to ignore.
**Don't** hand-roll a record list as a `<ul className="divide-y">` with its own row markup, or draw a status as a bespoke dot; use the Record lists components.
